svg.title: The daily loop, without GitHub
svg.desc: A comic strip of working with Git on your own PC, in eight steps. 1, 08:55, where am I: git status says you're on main with a clean working tree. Clean desk, clear head. 2, 09:00, side track: for a bigger task, git switch -c task/q3 gives it its own branch; for a small fix, skip this step. 3, 09:05, edit and save: work as usual in Word, Notepad or Power BI and press Ctrl+S; Git doesn't mind which program. 4, 11:25, check: git status and git diff show what changed, red out and green in. Look before you seal. 5, 11:30, commit: git add -A and git commit -m put the changes in the envelope and seal it with a note. Repeat steps 3 to 5 all day long. 6, next morning, review yourself: no pull request, so be your own reviewer with git diff main task/q3. Fresh eyes work best. 7, merge: on main, git merge --no-ff, then delete the branch. Your own Merge button. 8, Friday 17:00, back up: git push --all backup gives your history a second home. Laptop lost? Work isn't. Footer: steps 3 to 5 repeat all day; steps 1, 2, 6 and 7 once per task; step 8 once a week.
svg.text: Same rhythm as the team version. You're the author, the reviewer and the archivist.

g.text: A bigger task gets its own
the task stays visible as one loop
